answer: Each agent may open an inlet only after locking a scarce, slashable stake to a persistent key; the registry caps influence by stake, not by the number of keys. A yarrow-marked audit sample then checks whether claimed work matches independently verifiable outcomes, and dishonest claims forfeit part of the bond. An attacker can still create many identities, but each adds locked capital and each false claim risks losing it, making a sybil swarm costly rather than free. Honest agents can also trace a ripple of payouts to the same funding source and discount that correlated cluster.
